teams.heading: Italy's Leonardo Marin admits ill-discipline handed Fiji Udine win, vows Twickenham fix
teams.body: Fiji's 21-16 win in Udine was, by Leonardo Marin's account, a big chance Italy threw away. The Benetton centre said the Azzurri created plenty but squandered good try-scoring opportunities through errors, then conceded too many needless penalties that Fiji turned into a second-half gap. For the Twickenham rematch for 11th place, he wants Italy to hold the ball through more phases and gift nothing, warning the short turnaround makes physical preparation hard. Italy have called up Andrea Zambonin and Louis Lynagh.

lead.why: Fresh and forward-looking: Fiji's rematch opponent concedes Fiji punished Italy's discipline and sets out what must change for the 11th-place game.

teams.heading: Borthwick calls Saracens wing Noah Caluori into England training squad for rematch
teams.body: The only change to the 37-man group gathered at Pennyhill Park, Caluori faces a fight with Cadan Murley and Will Joseph for a matchday spot in Saturday's third-place play-off against New Zealand at Twickenham. Tommy Freeman pulled up with a niggle before last weekend's 37-12 win over the same opponents but remains in the squad. The rematch came about when France's victory over Argentina knocked England down to second on the table, one step short of the final.

lead.why: It is the only new England selection news before the All Blacks rematch.

teams.heading: France beat Argentina 45-17 as Antoine Dupont's scrum move yields two tries
teams.body: Antoine Dupont, not Matthieu Jalibert, ran the scrum launch that unlocked the Pumas in the 45-17 win at the Stade de France, Midi Olympique's breakdown shows. The same first-phase move put Mickaël Guillard over for the opening try and sent Émilien Gailleton in at the 64th minute for the bonus point that clinched a final against the Springboks. Kalvin Gourgues said Argentina's defence tended to narrow, especially near the line, which let France go wide by playing in behind.

lead.why: A fresh France match story: Dupont ran the move that produced the opening try and the bonus-point try that sealed the final.

teams.heading: Captain Dan Sheehan's yellow upgraded to red after Ireland beat Springboks 20-17
teams.body: Andy Farrell is sweating on his skipper before this week's Nations Championship finale against Australia at Twickenham. Sheehan was sin-binned for a croc-roll on Marco van Staden eight minutes from time on Saturday, before the foul play review officer made it a red, and the IRFU have yet to learn when his disciplinary hearing will be held. Otherwise there are no new injuries. "We've got a full squad of fit bodies, which is great," said assistant coach Andrew Goodman, with Farrell naming his matchday squad on Wednesday afternoon.

lead.why: The captain's upgraded red card and pending hearing is a fresh development hanging over the Australia selection.

teams.heading: Italy call up Zambonin and Lynagh for Twickenham rematch with Fiji
teams.body: Andrea Zambonin and Louis Lynagh have been added to Gonzalo Quesada's squad for the final week of camp in Udine, ahead of the Nations Championship play-off against Fiji at Twickenham for 11th place. Exeter lock Zambonin brings 21 caps, Benetton back-three man Lynagh 16. Federico Zanandrea and Giovanni Montemauri also return to the list. Both are uncapped, as are Mattia Midena and Damiano Mazza. Davide Sette joins as an invited player.

lead.why: Fresh squad news for the Twickenham rematch; the injury bulletin has already run.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham reaches 41 Scotland tries in 67-5 win over Japan
teams.body: Saturday's Nations Championship hat-trick at Murrayfield brought the wing's 39th, 40th and 41st international tries, extending his own Scotland record. He opened the scoring by hacking on after the visitors spilled Jamie Dobie's box-kick, and closed it in the 79th minute. Between those, he chased his own kick through and offloaded for Liam McConnell's second try, and Planet Rugby credited him with setting the tone in front of a 67,000 sell-out.

lead.why: Graham's try record is a fresh Scotland angle on the weekend, distinct from the McConnell and Townsend editions already run.

teams.heading: Tom Shanklin hails Eddie James a 'revelation' in Wales's emerging attack
teams.body: Speaking on BBC Scrum V, the former Wales centre said James had "been a revelation" since being thrown in at Test level, and predicted he would be "in that Welsh team for a long, long time as long as he's fit." James started all three November Tests, including Saturday's 26-29 defeat by Australia. Shanklin credited Matt Sherratt's attacking work and singled out Louis Rees-Zammit, who has scored in consecutive Tests after an eight-match drought.

lead.why: It is the freshest Wales story that is not another retelling of Tandy's rotation pledge, and it is pinned to a player who started every November Test.

teams.heading: Rugbyrama calls Pumas brave but largely devoid of talent in 45-17 loss
teams.body: France beat Argentina 45-17 at the Stade de France on Saturday, and Midi Olympique's Marc Duzan, writing for Rugbyrama, called the Pumas courageous but largely devoid of talent. His report conceded the visitors dominated the set scrum and answered Mickaël Guillard's opener through Justo Piccardo, Montpellier's hefty centre. France hooker Peato Mauvaka, interviewed by Rugbyrama, admitted frustration at the penalties his pack conceded at scrum time. Argentina's next assignment is Scotland at Twickenham, for seventh place.

lead.why: The Pumas-focused items already ran, so this takes a fresh Argentina angle: the French press verdict on the Pumas and their scrum dominance in Paris.

teams.heading: Ryan Lonergan tours Alpine F1 facility as Wallabies eye Ireland season-ender
teams.body: The scrum-half came away joking he might send his car over for a polish, but his focus is Ireland, who edged the Wallabies in Sydney in July when Ben Donaldson missed a penalty after the siren. Lonergan said Australia saw their game "start back up again" in the 29-26 win over Wales, which ended a four-game losing run, with "a few tidy-ups" still to make. "It’d be a good way to round out the Nations Championship with a win," he added.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy vows to rotate Wales for injury-stretched Japan's Twickenham finale
teams.body: Japan's November closes against Wales at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium on Saturday. They may face a different side from the one that spluttered past Eddie Jones' men in Cardiff. Wales coach Steve Tandy, eyeing next year's World Cup, said: "I can rotate the team and we'll still put in a performance." Former Lions wing Alex Cuthbert wants the frontliners kept in to "really put Japan to the sword". The BBC reports Japan are stretched by injury and conceded 24 tries in defeats by England and Scotland.

teams.heading: All Blacks lose Luke Jacobson to Bayonne after 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Bayonne announced a three-year deal on Monday for the 29-year-old loose forward, who has spent his whole career with the Chiefs and Waikato. All Blacks selection requires an NZR contract and play in the domestic system, so the move ends his Test availability once next year's tournament is done. Known as "Concrete Shoulders" for his tackling, Jacobson has 30 Tests. The latest was against Ireland in Auckland in July's Nations Championship leg, and he played three matches on the run to the 2023 World Cup final.

lead.why: The only new New Zealand event in today's coverage; the Rennie backing and the England post-mortems have already run.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus makes seven changes, starts Libbok and Reinach for France final
teams.body: With Damian Willemse out with an ankle injury, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu shifts to full-back for Sunday's Nations Championship final at Twickenham, Manie Libbok takes the No. 10 jersey and Cobus Reinach starts at scrum-half, a half-back pairing straight out of the 2023 World Cup run. Up front, Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit start, Salmaan Moerat is recalled for a first appearance since July 2025, and Eben Etzebeth drops to the bench. Emmanuel Tshituka is in line for a debut among the replacements.

lead.why: The Springbok team for the Nations Championship final is a fresh selection event, and the previous editions have not covered it.
